name: Luxembourg
summary: Luxembourg does not tax a resident's gains on shares and bonds held longer than six months, provided the holding is not a 'material interest' (more than 10% of a company within the last five years). Dividends from qualifying (EU, Luxembourg and treaty-country) companies are 50% exempt, giving a top rate of about 22.9%; other investment income is taxed at up to 45.78%. There is no wealth tax for individuals (abolished 2006). Children who inherit their legal share from a Luxembourg-resident parent pay no inheritance tax; only amounts above the legal share are taxed (2.5%/5% plus surcharges). Notarial gifts to children cost 1.8% registration duty, while hand-to-hand gifts of movables (e.g. securities transfers) are not registered and not taxed unless the donor dies in the same year.

regimes.name: Ordinary tax residence
regimes.description: Resident individuals are taxed on worldwide income at progressive rates (top 42% plus 9% solidarity surcharge = 45.78%), with exemptions for long-term private gains on non-material holdings and a 50% dividend exemption.
regimes.eligibility: Habitual abode (an effectively used home) in Luxembourg, or a stay of more than six consecutive months. Non-EU citizens need a residence permit.

capital_gains.summary: Gains on shares, bonds and other movable assets held more than six months are tax-free unless the seller holds a material interest (more than 10% of the company, alone or with household, at any time in the five years before the sale). Gains within six months are speculative and taxed at progressive rates up to 45.78% (if total speculative gains exceed EUR 500 a year). A material interest sold after six months is taxed at half the average rate, at most 22.89%. Real estate (not the main home) sold within five years is taxed at progressive rates; after five years at half the global rate (at most 22.89%), after an allowance of up to EUR 50,000 per 10 years (doubled for couples).
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: Speculative gains below EUR 500 a year exempt. Main residence exempt. Real estate allowance EUR 50,000 per 10 years (EUR 100,000 for jointly taxed couples), plus up to EUR 75,000 for property inherited in the direct line.
capital_gains.eligibility_conditions: Private investor holding below 10% of each company and holding more than six months.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: The speculative period for real estate was extended from two to five years for sales after 2024. Derivatives settled in cash and frequent short-term trading are likely taxed as speculative or business income. A former non-resident who becomes resident: material-interest gains are computed from market value on arrival only in specific cases (not verified). No exit tax for individuals on private portfolios.

sources.title: Luxembourg - Individual - Taxes on personal income

open_questions: Only a professional source (PwC, reviewed 3 August 2026) was opened; the income tax law (LIR arts. 99bis, 99ter, 100) was not re-read.
Treatment of material-interest gains for newly arrived residents (step-up of acquisition cost) not verified.
capital_gains.rate_basis: Top income tax rate 42% (from EUR 234,870 taxable income, 2025 scale) x 1.09 solidarity surcharge = 45.78% headline (short-term gains). Listed securities held over six months and below 10%: exempt (0). Material interest held over six months: half the global rate, capped at 22.89%. Real estate held over five years: half the global rate, top 22.89% (before the allowance). Foreign real estate: Luxembourg's rate shown; most treaties give the situs country the right to tax and Luxembourg exempts with progression.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Frequent short-term trading, leverage and derivatives raise the risk of being treated as carrying on a business, making all gains taxable at progressive rates. Administrative guidance for individuals is limited; a ruling can be sought.
capital_gains.holding_period_rules: Movable assets: six months. Real estate: five years (two years before 2025).
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Worldwide taxation; foreign securities treated like domestic ones.

dividends.summary: Dividends are taxed at progressive rates, but half of the dividend is exempt if paid by a fully taxable Luxembourg company, an EU company covered by the Parent-Subsidiary Directive, or a company resident in a treaty country and subject to comparable tax. At the top rate that is 22.89%. Other dividends are taxed in full (up to 45.78%). A EUR 1,500 investment income deduction applies (EUR 3,000 for couples). Luxembourg companies withhold 15%, which is credited.
dividends.exemptions_thresholds: EUR 1,500 investment income deduction (doubled for jointly taxed couples); 50% exemption for qualifying dividends. Interest paid by Luxembourg paying agents bears a final 20% withholding (relibi).
dividends.eligibility_conditions: Payer must be a qualifying company as described.
dividends.important_exceptions: Dividends from companies in non-treaty or low-tax countries, and fund distributions, do not get the 50% exemption.

sources.title: Luxembourg - Individual - Taxes on personal income
Circulaire n° 823 SPF (changes to the SPF law from 1 January 2025)
sources.publisher: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA

open_questions: The exact list of qualifying payers for the 50% exemption (art. 115 no. 15a LIR) was not re-read; whether US companies qualify depends on the 'comparable tax' test, generally accepted in practice.
dividends.rate_basis: 45.78% top rate x 50% taxable = 22.89% on qualifying dividends (domestic and treaty-country companies). Foreign withholding tax is credited against Luxembourg tax on that income, within treaty limits; with a 15% foreign withholding the extra Luxembourg tax is about 7.9 points.
dividends.withholding_outbound: 15% on dividends paid by Luxembourg companies (0% under the participation exemption or to EU parent companies; reduced by treaty). No withholding on interest or liquidation proceeds. SPFs and investment funds do not withhold.
dividends.treaty_network: About 85 income tax treaties, including the US and all EU states.
dividends.holding_company_notes: Soparfi (ordinary company): 23.87% combined rate in Luxembourg City (2025/2026), full participation exemption for holdings of at least 10% or EUR 1.2 million held 12 months, 0.5% net wealth tax at company level. SPF (family wealth management company): exempt from income tax, 0.25% subscription tax on paid-up capital plus share premium (minimum EUR 1,000 from 2025, maximum EUR 125,000 a year), no treaty access, passive holding only. No structure is modelled: a resident already pays 0% on portfolio gains held over six months and about 22.9% on dividends, while a Soparfi pays 23.87% on portfolio gains and dividends plus 0.5% net wealth tax, and an SPF costs 0.25% a year (EUR 75,000 on EUR 30 million), loses treaty relief, and its distributions are fully taxable at up to 45.78% without the 50% exemption.

wealth_tax.summary: No wealth tax for individuals, resident or non-resident, since 1 January 2006. (Companies pay net wealth tax.)
wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Municipal property tax on the old unitary value (assessment rate 0.7%-1% x communal multiplier 200%-800%); low in practice. A property tax reform is under discussion.

inheritance.summary: Inheritance tax applies only if the deceased was a Luxembourg resident (domicile and centre of activities); the heirs' residence does not matter. Children are exempt on their legal share of the estate. Anything a child receives above the legal share (through a will) is taxed at 2.5%, and the surplus at 5%, with surcharges when the taxable portion exceeds EUR 10,000. A family that divides the estate equally among the three children pays nothing. Spouses are exempt.
inheritance.exemptions_thresholds: Direct line: legal share 0%. Estates below EUR 1,250 exempt.
inheritance.eligibility_conditions: Exemption applies to the legal (intestate) share of each child. Non-resident decedents: only Luxembourg real estate is taxed (transfer duty at the same rates); Luxembourg bank accounts and securities of a non-resident are not taxed.
inheritance.important_exceptions: Bequests to children above their legal share: 2.5% / 5% base rates multiplied by surcharges (up to 2.2x) for larger portions; the official page gives an example of a 140% increase. Foreign real estate and movables are taxed with reference to the deceased's citizenship rules (PwC).

sources.title: How to calculate taxes on an inherited estate

open_questions: The guichet.lu inheritance page was last updated in 2019 and the gift page says it is being updated; confirm current rates with the AED.
The full surcharge scale for amounts above the legal share is on the AED portal and was not opened.

Whether a hand-to-hand transfer of a securities account is reliably outside registration duty should be confirmed with a Luxembourg notary; PwC says such gifts attract no tax unless the donor dies in the same civil year.
inheritance.gift_tax: Gifts by notarial deed bear registration duty on market value: 1.8% for gifts to children that count as an advance on the inheritance, 2.4% for gifts outside the share; plus 1% register fee for Luxembourg real estate (and a 50% surtax in Luxembourg City on real estate other than single-family homes). Hand-to-hand gifts of movables need no deed and are not taxed unless the donor dies in the same calendar year.
inheritance.business_relief: Not needed for direct-line legal shares.
inheritance.foreign_assets: Worldwide estate of a resident decedent within scope; for non-residents only Luxembourg real estate.
inheritance.domicile_rules: Depends only on the deceased's residence (domicile and centre of activities in Luxembourg). The heir's residence is irrelevant for inheritance tax; for gift duty the parties' residence is irrelevant and duty arises when a deed is registered in Luxembourg.

residency.tax_residency_test: Resident if the person has an effectively used abode in Luxembourg or stays more than six consecutive months (also across two years or with short absences).

routes.name: EU/EEA/Swiss free movement
routes.requirements: Declaration of arrival at the commune; registration certificate after three months.

routes.name: Residence permit for investors or private reasons
routes.requirements: Luxembourg offers a residence permit for investors (investment in a Luxembourg company, a new business, or a large deposit in a Luxembourg financial institution) and a permit for private reasons for people with sufficient resources. Thresholds were not verified in this session.

corporate.summary: Corporate income tax 16% (14% below EUR 175,000) plus 7% solidarity surtax plus 6.75% municipal business tax in Luxembourg City = 23.87% combined (from tax year 2025; 24.94% before). Participation exemption for holdings of at least 10% or EUR 1.2 million (EUR 6 million for gains) held 12 months. Companies pay 0.5% net wealth tax. Pillar Two applies to large groups.
corporate.special_zones: SPF family wealth company: no income tax, 0.25% subscription tax, passive holding only.

Asking rents excluding charges, not achieved rents.

us_citizen_notes: US-Luxembourg income tax treaty applies; there is no estate tax treaty. Luxembourg's 0% on long-term gains means US citizens pay full US capital gains tax with no foreign credit. Non-US funds and SPFs raise PFIC/CFC issues.
open_questions: Impatriate regime (reformed from 1 January 2025: 50% exemption of salary up to EUR 400,000, minimum base salary EUR 75,000) applies only to employment income and is not modelled as a special regime.
A single tax class reform is expected from tax year 2028 (PwC); not in force.
2026 income tax brackets: PwC shows the 2025 indexed scale; any 2026 indexation was not confirmed.
Investor residence permit thresholds not verified (guichet.lu page not found).
Prime rent is a single-day sample of 15 asking rents on one portal; a Luxembourg agency report or the Observatoire de l'Habitat rent series would be a better long-run source.
